findings.note: Flipping the right pair to lightning:encore gives the same 'danger/rule prevents event' relation as curfew:finale, so a player reading it this way would feel it solves cleanly. Both halves read as: "curfew prevents finale (cause -> prevented event)" and "lightning prevents encore, read as lightning:encore (cause -> prevented event)".

notes:
set-prevention allows a valid cross-reading swap (curfew:finale / lightning:encore) because curfew/lightning are both generic causes and encore/finale are near-synonymous, creating a genuine alternate solution. Replace one pair with words that break the symmetry.
- set-prevention: Lightning/curfew are both generic show-stopping causes and encore/finale are near-synonymous show-endings, so the pairs can be cross-matched (curfew:finale, lightning:encore) into an equally valid reading.
  Try: Replace 'finale' with a non-synonymous prevented event tied specifically to a rule, e.g. 'curfew : encore' :: 'rainout : ceremony' — pick a cause/event pair where the cause type differs sharply in kind from lightning (rule vs weather) so no cross-swap reads naturally.
  Or: Keep curfew:encore, but replace lightning:finale with a pair where the prevented event is not an ending at all, e.g. 'flood : rehearsal', so encore and the new event aren't near-synonyms.
  Or: Replace both right-side words to widen semantic distance: 'blackout : intermission' — ensure the two prevented-events (encore vs intermission) and two causes (curfew vs blackout) are not mutually substitutable.
Do not change: set-taxonomic, set-agent-instrument, set-defective — no allowlisted finding touches them.
